summary: The note is a Wikipedia-style overview of the Cricket World Cup, covering the record of host nations and the teams that have done best or worst while co-hosting. It also explains the tournament's qualification structure, the number of teams and editions, the list of past winners, and its standing among world sporting events.
one_line: Overview of the Cricket World Cup, covering host-nation results, qualification, past winners, and its ranking among world sporting events.
key_facts: Sri Lanka, as co-host of the 1996 Cricket World Cup, was the first host to win the tournament, though the final was held in Pakistan.
India won the 2011 tournament as host and was the first team to win a final played in their own country.
Australia repeated the feat of winning as host in 2015.
England is the only other host to have made the final, in 1979.
New Zealand achieved their best World Cup result while co-hosting in 2015 as finalists.
Zimbabwe reached the Super Six while co-hosting in 2003, and Kenya reached the semi-finals in 2003 while co-hosting.
In 1987, co-hosts India and Pakistan both reached the semi-finals, but were eliminated by Australia and England respectively.
Australia in 1992, England in 1999, South Africa in 2003, and Bangladesh in 2011 were host teams eliminated in the first round.
The World Cup is open to all members of the International Cricket Council (ICC), although the highest-ranking teams receive automatic qualification.
The remaining teams are determined via the World Cricket League and the ICC World Cup Qualifier.
A total of twenty teams have competed in the eleven editions of the tournament.
Fourteen teams competed in the 2015 edition, and the 2019 edition will have only ten teams.
Australia has won the tournament five times, while the West Indies, India (twice each), Pakistan and Sri Lanka (once each) have also won it.
The best performance by a non-full-member team came when Kenya made the semi-finals of the 2003 tournament.
The tournament is the world's 4th biggest sporting event, behind the FIFA World Cup, Summer Olympics and Rugby World Cup.
